Mitchell invests \$600 000 for 8 years at $4.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.

Calculate the value of his investment after 8 years.

solutions.latex:
Using the compound interest formula:
$$\begin{aligned} FV&=PV(1+r)^n\\ &=600\,000(1+4.5\%)^8\\ &=\$853\,260.37\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: The cost of the weekly groceries for the Stewart family in January 2016 was \$228.00. Since 2016, the inflation rate in Australia has averaged at $1.9\%$ p.a. If this rate continues, what will be the cost of their weekly groceries in January 2020?

solutions.latex:
There are 4 years from January 2016 to January 2020.
$$\begin{aligned} FV&=228.00\times(1+1.9\%)^4\\ &\approx\$245.83\end{aligned}$$
This matches option D.

parts.latex:
Peter invests \$26 000 in an account that pays $5.4\%$ p.a. interest, compounded quarterly.

Which calculation would give the value of the investment after 18 months?

solutions.latex:
18 months is 6 quarters.

The quarterly rate is $5.4\% \div 4 = 1.35\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 26000 \times (1 + 1.35\%)^6 \\ &= 26000 \times (1.0135)^6 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is option D.

parts.latex: In July 2020, the inflation rate in a certain country was reported to be $4.1\%$ per day. If a chocolate bar costs \$2.50 today, what will its price be 90 days from now if its price increases in line with the inflation rate in that country?

solutions.latex:
Using the future value formula $FV = PV(1 + r)^n$:
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 2.50(1 + 0.041)^{90} \\ &= 93.0048\ldots \\ &\approx \$93.00 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore \text{the chocolate bar costs } \$93.00 \text{ in 90 days}$$
